conf.description: Linux auditd, auditd, syslog-raw: hand-built key=value pipeline (no vendor pack exists); regex_extract splits the audit(epoch.msec:seq) header from the kv body, serde kvp parses the body, code reassembles EXECVE a0..aN into process.args (in-record only, no cross-record join) with hex/escape decode and best-effort credential-arg masking per recommendations.direct.cribl, eval implements the mapped/partial transforms.

conf.comment: linux-auditd/auditd/syslog-raw. No vendor pack parses raw auditd key=value records. EXECVE a0..aN reassembly into process.args happens WITHIN this one line only (all argv fields are already on the same EXECVE record); joining that EXECVE record to its sibling SYSCALL/USER_AUTH record by shared msgid is cross-event stateful correlation, which the brief's join-function constraints put out of scope for a Cribl pipeline. Per recommendations.direct.cribl, this pipeline instead stamps auditd.log.msgid (epoch.msec:seq from the audit(...) header) on every record so Elastic can reassemble multi-record events downstream.

functions.description: identify technology, dataset, format, and parsing approach

split the audit(epoch.msec:seq) msgid header (type=, msg=audit(...):) from the remaining key=value body so the body can be parsed generically and the msgid components are available for a correlation id
parse the remaining key=value pairs (arch=, syscall=, exe="...", comm="...", pid=, uid=, key="...", a0="..."..., addr=, terminal=, hostname=, ...) into top-level fields

conf.code: function auditdDecode(v) { if (typeof v !== 'string') return v; if (/^[0-9A-Fa-f]{2,}$/.test(v) && v.length % 2 === 0) {   var out = '';   for (var i = 0; i < v.length; i += 2) { out += String.fromCharCode(parseInt(v.substr(i, 2), 16)); }   return out; } return v;}if (__e['exe'] !== undefined) { __e['exe'] = auditdDecode(__e['exe']); }if (__e['comm'] !== undefined) { __e['comm'] = auditdDecode(__e['comm']); }if (__e['key'] !== undefined) { __e['key'] = auditdDecode(__e['key']); }if (__e['audit_type'] === 'EXECVE') {  var args = [];  for (var i = 0; i < 64; i++) {    var k = 'a' + i;    if (__e[k] === undefined) break;    args.push(auditdDecode(__e[k]));  }  for (var j = 0; j < args.length; j++) {    if (typeof args[j] === 'string' && /^-p.+/.test(args[j])) { args[j] = '-pREDACTED'; }    else if (args[j] === '-p' || args[j] === '-u') { if (args[j+1] !== undefined) { args[j+1] = 'REDACTED'; } }    else if (args[j] === 'sshpass') { if (args[j+1] === '-p' && args[j+2] !== undefined) { args[j+2] = 'REDACTED'; } }  }  if (args.length) { __e['process.args'] = args; }}

functions.description: decode auditd's escaped/hex string encoding on exe, comm, key, and each EXECVE argv token; reassemble a0..aN (present together on one EXECVE line, no cross-record join needed) into an ordered process.args array; best-effort redact credential-bearing argv tokens (mysql -p<pw>, sshpass -p <pw>, curl -u <user:pass>) per recommendations.direct.cribl's data-hygiene instruction

implement the transforms that need the original vendor names before rename: success yes/no to event.outcome, key split into rule.name (auditd joins multiple -k keys with a single 0x01 SOH byte, per the linux-audit convention, not a printable delimiter), numeric casts for syscall/auid, hostname-vs-IP check for source.domain, msgid correlation id for downstream Elastic reassembly, and _time from the audit(epoch.msec:seq) header rather than syslog receipt time
batch-rename the status:mapped fields that need no further transform, once the transforms above have already read their original vendor names
